sites.name: Connecting ridge
sites.point: Point C1 of Gläser et al. 2018 (same spot as Gläser et al. 2014 CR1 spot 2)
sites.source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162
sites.notes: Published 88.0% mean solar illumination at 2 m, 2017–2037. Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 pathfinder targets the Shackleton connecting ridge (no coordinates published).

sites.name: Shackleton rim
sites.point: Shackleton rim point of Gläser et al. 2018
sites.source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162
sites.notes: Published 85.5% mean solar illumination at 2 m, 2017–2037.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus landing site
sites.point: Where Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander came to rest on 22 Feb 2024
sites.source: NASA LRO image release, Feb 2024; LROC image release 1360
sites.notes: Odysseus landed tilted in a degraded 1 km crater near Malapert A, on a local slope of about 12°, and worked for about a week. North of 83°S, so its nearest map is the 20 m one.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena landing site
sites.point: Where Intuitive Machines' Athena lander came to rest on 6 Mar 2025
sites.notes: Athena landed on its side in a small crater about 250 m from its target.

sites.name: VIPER mission area
sites.point: Center of VIPER's planned mission area (about 5 × 4 km)
sites.notes: VIPER is now scheduled on Blue Origin's second Blue Moon MK1 (CLPS task order CS-7, late 2027). NASA has not confirmed whether this area is kept.

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor
sites.point: Lowest LOLA point within 3 km of the IAU crater center (89.67°S, 129.78°E); set by scripts/sites.py
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature; LOLA 10 m map
sites.notes: Permanently shadowed. Included to contrast with the sunlit rim a few kilometres away.
